images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Original final production environment for a scrolling overhead WWII Adriatic naval arcade game. Wide landscape 3:2 tile. Strictly vertical 90-degree orthographic map view from directly above; roofs and water surfaces only, no sky or horizon or perspective. Quiet, beautiful hand-pixeled 1990s simulation art with economical pixel clusters, readable flat areas, restrained natural water texture and blocky stone/scrub detail. Horizontal direction of travel. No boats, people, weapons, gun emplacements, projectiles, lettering, HUD, symbols, wakes, wrecks, flags, modern buildings or modern infrastructure. Art is a scenic interpretation in May 1944, not a labeled map. No decorative border. Night departure from the old Dalmatian harbour of Vis on the island of Vis. Across the entire TOP 18% is the land, with a pale limestone quay, a few tightly cropped small Dalmatian tiled roofs, tiny wooden crates and a few discreet amber lamps in deep indigo surroundings. Its southern water edge tracks a roughly horizontal line at 18% of image height with only slight variations so it can be measured. Do not insert piers into the navigable channel. Across the entire BOTTOM 13% is a separate low dark rocky headland with Mediterranean scrub; its northern edge approximately horizontal. The broad central 69% is uninterrupted calm night water in muted navy-indigo with the faintest blue reflections. Vary the shore composition across x, keep left and right ends open for scrolling, make the difference between land and water recognizable even at night.
